subject: Post-call: CardioSync streaming behavior & model fit next steps
messages:
From: Samir Gupta <sgupta@cardiosync.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: elena.torres@cardiosync.com
Date: 2027-03-05T15:20:00Z
Subject: Thanks — discovery recap and streaming concerns

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the call today — it was helpful to run through our intended flows. A quick recap from our side and a couple of clarifying points: 

- Use case: real-time physician assistant for cardiology clinics. Short prompts (20-80 tokens) followed by streaming completion for structured guidance and follow-up actions.
- SLOs: 95th pct latency <= 300ms for partial tokens in the first 800 tokens; overall session latency budget ~1s.
- Key quality issue we saw in our prototype: partial outputs occasionally truncate mid-sentence or produce incoherent trailing fragments when the model is streamed (stop sequences are applied client-side today).

We'd like Redwood's recommended models and a proposed eval plan focusing on (a) partial-output coherence, (b) stop-sequence adherence, and (c) token-level latency under our load profile. Also — examples attached that show the trailing fragments (streaming-coherence-examples.txt).

Next steps from our side: share access to a synthetic prompt set you can use for a sandbox run. I attached the first pass (cardiosync-promptset-v1.txt). Can Redwood turn that into a short benchmark (sample runs + metrics) we can review next week?

Thanks,
Samir
Senior Product Manager
CardioSync

--
Attachment: cardiosync-promptset-v1.txt (text)
Attachment: streaming-coherence-examples.txt (text)

From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: Samir Gupta <sgupta@cardiosync.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-03-05T19:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Thanks — discovery recap and streaming concerns

Samir — great notes and thank you for the artifacts. We can absolutely run a targeted streaming evaluation against your prompt set. Initial thoughts / proposals below.

Short summary of what we'll run:
- Model candidates: redwood/titan-70b-fp16 (baseline for coherence), open-13b-q4 (cost-efficient comparison), and redwood/stream-7b (tuned for low-latency streaming).
- Eval axes: partial-output coherence (BLEU + human spot checks on trailing fragments), stop-sequence fidelity (false-positive/false-negative stop triggers), token-latency distribution (p50/p95/p99 for first 800 tokens), and cost per session estimate.
- Testbed config: simulated 10tps sustained, burst to 30tps to capture autoscale effects; sequence lengths per your distribution (mean 420 tokens).

Immediate asks from Redwood engineering: a short list of 10 representative prompts from your file marked HIGH priority that cause the most problematic partial outputs. If you can flag them inline we’ll prioritize.

Proposed timeline:
- Tue (48h): We ingest prompt set and run smoke streaming against redwood/stream-7b and open-13b-q4 (rough latency + qualitative check).
- Fri (EOD): Deliver a short report with sample recordings (stream logs + token timings), and a recommendation (canary config + suggested stop-sequence handling).

I’m cc'ing Ben and Marissa to scope the evaluation artifacts and to propose any quick product-level mitigations (client-side stop handling, buffering strategy).

Thanks — will confirm calendar invite for a 30-minute review after the Friday drop.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

--
Attachment: initial-eval-plan.xlsx (spreadsheet, stub)

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Samir Gupta <sgupta@cardiosync.com>
Date: 2027-03-06T01:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Thanks — discovery recap and streaming concerns

Looping in a couple of quick technical checks we'll run during the smoke tests and what to capture in the report: 

- Token-level timestamps for each partial chunk (this will show where p95 spikes occur). Include both model-side and gateway-side latencies.
- KV cache warm vs cold behavior — partial coherence issues commonly surface at cache-warm boundaries for multi-turn sessions.
- Stop-sequence enforcement: instrument both model-run-level stop triggers and gateway post-processing to measure discrepancies.
- Edge case: streaming + client-side stop tokens causing mid-stream truncation; we'll test both server-enforced and client-enforced stop modes.

Ben
Sr. Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Samir Gupta <sgupta@cardiosync.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: Elena Torres <elena.torres@cardiosync.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2027-03-06T14:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Thanks — discovery recap and streaming concerns

Perfect — thanks, team. A few clarifications based on Ben's list: 

- Latency: p95 for first-token is our biggest gating item. We can accept occasional p99s but p95 must be below 300ms.
- Examples: I've pasted two short transcripts from our prototype below that show (a) trailing fragment after the dot and (b) stop-sequence misfire where the client saw "[END]" in the middle of a sentence.

--- transcript #1 (prototype stream) ---
Physician: "Patient presents with chest pain, prior MI, on metoprolol. Next steps?"
Assistant (partial streaming chunk): "Recommend immediate ECG, obtain troponin labs, continue beta-blocker. Consider urgent cath if..."
Assistant (later chunk): "... symptoms worsen. [END]"
Assistant (post-END fragment): "ly re-evaluate for surgical consultation."

--- transcript #2 (stop misfire) ---
Assistant streamed: "If ischemia is suspected, ensure oxygen, nitroglycerin as needed. [END] however consider serial enzymes..."

We can annotate more cases if useful.

Also — regarding model choices, cost is a concern for us. If open-13b-q4 shows comparable coherence with significantly lower cost, that's preferable, but we want to see the metrics.

We'll be waiting for the smoke-run results. If possible, can the Friday report include sample streamed recordings we can replay in our UI? That would be super helpful.

Thanks,
Samir

--
Attachment: streaming-coherence-examples.txt (already shared)

From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: Samir Gupta <sgupta@cardiosync.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-03-08T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Thanks — discovery recap and streaming concerns (next steps + calendar)

Samir — quick status and concrete next steps: 

1) We've ingested cardiosync-promptset-v1 and flagged 12 HIGH-priority prompts (see folder in Drive).
2) Running smoke tests now against redwood/stream-7b and open-13b-q4. Ben's team is capturing token timestamps and stop-event deltas; expected artifacts: token-timing CSVs, streaming mp4 captures of the client UI replay, and a short qualitative note deck.
3) Friday EOD (2027-03-12) deliverable: short report + recommendation (canary config + 2-tier model suggestion) and a cost delta table.
4) Proposed canary: start with redwood/stream-7b in a 5% production canary with server-side stop enforcement + gateway buffering (250ms batching window), fallback to open-13b-q4 if p95 > 350ms or coherence regressions > 7% on the annotated set.

Calendar: I created a 30-minute review slot for Mon 2027-03-15 10:00-10:30 PT — invite should land in your inbox (HubSpot link and Drive link included below). If that doesn't work, propose an alternate.

Deliverables attached/linked: prompt set (uploaded), initial-eval-plan.xlsx (test matrix), and a shared Drive with results: https://drive.example/redwood/cardiosync/eval-artifacts

If CardioSync wants to accelerate, we can also do an isolated private sandbox run on dedicated capacity for a 24-hour window — cost estimate included in the Friday report.

Thanks — looking forward to the results.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
